summary:
The SCTE-35 survey for Phase 3 (§3.1, as D-070 scopes it) is written. No Phase 3 code was written, and the worktree is unchanged at 75cf6e0 (git status is clean).

The survey (scte35.md) covers each D-070 tag's syntax as vendors print it, the splice_info_section layout down to the fields Phase 3 needs, how each HLS form places a cue in media time, what Mirage parses today, what FFmpeg 8.1.1's hls demuxer exposes, and the public VOD streams found. It closes with design options for the owner (labelled agent's recommendations, nothing decided) and the differences from D-070.

scte35_vectors.json holds 79 SCTE-35 messages copied by pattern from 15 citable sources, each with its URL or commit, licence, locator and the decoded fields the source gives. Each also has the result of the agent's own decoder check, labelled as such. That decoder was written from SCTE 35 2023r1's tables and matches every field the sources state for:
- all 8 of the standard's §14 sample messages;
- scte35-go's 11 positive test cases;
- threefive's 3 documented decodes.

Every number in the survey comes from a saved run (command, date and full output under scte35_evidence/runs/) or from a cited source. tools/pipeline.sh reruns every step after the fetches.

scte.org returned HTTP 403, so the standard was read from the copy committed in Comcast/scte35-go. One attempt with a different User-Agent was blocked by the permission system and not retried. The newer SCTE 35-1 2023r2 and 35-2 2026 were not read.
key_findings: Three signalings beyond D-070's list are in use. (1) #EXT-X-SCTE35, the only HLS tag the SCTE 35 standard itself defines (SCTE 35 2023r1 §12.2.2-12.2.4, Tables 30-31, pp. 107-110). (2) #EXT-X-SPLICEPOINT-SCTE35 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/hls-ad-markers.html; https://developers.broadpeak.io/docs/dai-scte35). (3) Adobe's #EXT-X-CUE (MediaLive's 'Adobe' style at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/medialive/latest/ug/sample-manifests-hls.html; https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/13049027; Adobe's PSDK page). Reported for the owner in scte35.md §9, not decided.

The non-standard tags have no specification and each vendor prints its own variants. EXT-X-CUE-OUT appears bare, as :30.000, :DURATION=120, :10.50,K=V, and :ID="...",X-TYPE="EABN",DURATION=29.988. CUE-OUT-CONT appears as '8.308/30' or as 'ElapsedTime=..,Duration=..,SCTE35=..'. CUE-IN appears bare or as CUE-IN:ID="..." (Google Video Stitcher). Every variant is quoted with its URL in scte35.md §2, and 118 tag lines are in scte35_vectors.json (hls_tag_lines).

A cue can be placed in media time three ways: the tag's position, DATERANGE START-DATE mapped through PROGRAM-DATE-TIME, or the splice PTS in the message ((pts_time + pts_adjustment) mod 2^33; SCTE 35 §9.6.1 p. 41, §9.8.1.1 p. 57). Vendors disagree on which counts: MediaTailor ignores START-DATE, Video Stitcher applies a DATERANGE to the next segment 'even when the START-DATE does not match', and broadpeak.io takes OATCLS start times from PDT and position, 'not taken from the payload'. In Wowza's published example a DATERANGE START-DATE falls 13.8 s after its tag's position (runs/cue_positions.txt). Several published messages carry no splice PTS at all (Unified's, broadpeak's OATCLS, Video Stitcher's), per runs/check_vectors.txt.

Layout checked: tools/scte35_decode.py, written from SCTE 35 2023r1 Tables 5, 9-15, 17-20, 27 and 28, matches the SCTE §14 samples, scte35-go and threefive. All 8 of the standard's §14 samples have a valid CRC_32 and agree with 26, 22, 25, 40, 25, 40, 25 and 55 listed fields. scte35-go's 11 positive cases and threefive's 3 decodes agree with no mismatch (runs/check_vectors.txt).

Many published examples are not valid messages. Of 79 vectors, 61 decode with a valid CRC and no disagreement with their source, 9 have a bad CRC_32 and 9 do not decode (3 of each kind are scte35-go's intended negative tests) [erratum, 2026-11-02: 1 of the 9 with a bad CRC_32 and 3 of the 9 that don't decode are, scte35_evidence/runs/check_vectors.txt:39, 40, 44, 47; review-3/runs/vector-status.txt]. The failures are:
- RFC 8216 §8.10: both examples one byte short of their section_length.
- draft-pantos-hls-rfc8216bis-22 §9.10: CRC_32 = 0x00000000.
- Google Cloud Video Stitcher: all 3 examples fail the CRC.
- Wowza: both DATERANGE values lack their CRC bytes.
- Unified's docs: 2 examples with a bad CRC, 1 printed cut short.
- Google Ad Manager: 1 cut short, 1 bad CRC.
(runs/check_vectors.txt; agent_check in scte35_vectors.json)

Example of pts_adjustment wrapping: broadpeak.io's and Google Ad Manager's 'Splice Cue' message has a pts_adjustment and a pts_time whose sum wraps past 2^33 (runs/check_vectors.txt). The CRC is CRC-32/MPEG-2. With FFmpeg's library API it is checked as av_crc(av_crc_get_table(AV_CRC_32_IEEE), UINT32_MAX, section, len) == 0, as FFmpeg's mpegts.c:463 does; crc.c:341 defines that table as 0x04C11DB7, not reflected (n8.1.1).

Mirage today, shown by running the repository's own unchanged ManifestParser and HlsAlign objects on published playlists (runs/parser_probe.txt):
- ManifestParser.cpp:320-322 (starts_with "#EXT-X-CUE-OUT") turns every CUE-OUT-CONT into a CueOut: 7 CueOut for 2 breaks.
- #EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35 is dropped entirely, because the unknown-tag branch at :328 needs the #EXT-X- prefix.
- '#EXT-X-CUE-IN:ID=...' becomes Unknown (:324-326).
- EXT-X-DATERANGE is Unknown, with no attribute parsing.
- A tag between #EXTINF and its URI gets the end of its segment (:340-344): Wowza's CUE-OUT lands at 38.700 s for a segment starting at 35.000 s.
- disc_seq is not incremented at EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY (:302-310).
- Nothing in src/ decodes a splice_info_section (runs/repo_grep.txt).
- hls::parse_media_timeline ignores cue tags (HlsAlign.cpp:521-569), but its Segment already has start, pdt, disc_seq and line (HlsAlign.h:33-47).
- mirage_vmaf reads no media-playlist tags (VMAFLadder.cpp:3,162).

FFmpeg n8.1.1's hls demuxer gives its caller no cue tag and no DATERANGE. parse_playlist handles 11 tags (libavformat/hls.c:861-988) and skips every other '#' line with av_log(AV_LOG_VERBOSE, "Skip ('%s')") (hls.c:989-991; runs/grep-hls.c-tags.txt), so Phase 3 must read the playlist text itself. By code reading only (not run): mpegts.c turns a PMT stream of type 0x86 with a CUEI registration into an AV_CODEC_ID_SCTE_35 data stream (mpegts.c:2522-2526, 2700-2703, 1790-1816). hls.c's update_streams_from_subdemuxer then forwards every substream (hls.c:2071-2090).

Only one public VOD stream with SCTE-35 was found: Unified Streaming's Remix AVOD demo origin, which generates the playlist on request.
- It is VOD (EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:VOD and EXT-X-ENDLIST).
- Its three renditions carry identical DATERANGE SCTE35-OUT, EXT-X-CUE-OUT:30 and EXT-X-CUE-IN lines, plus PDT (runs/hls_tags-streams.txt, runs/same_daterange.txt). The DATERANGE message is an immediate splice_insert whose break_duration equals its PLANNED-DURATION.
- The segments' first video PTS are 900000 and 1800000, so media time = playlist time + 10 s (runs/ts_probe-unified-avod.txt).
- The cue's segment also carries the same section as an ID3 PRIV frame owned by urn:scte:scte35:2013:bin, at PTS 1800000 (runs/ts_pid35-unified-avod-seg6.txt).
The other streams were excluded: Unified's live SCTE-35 demos are live, and Mux's dai-discontinuity test stream is AES-128 encrypted and carries no SCTE-35 tags.

Sources: scte.org returned HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch (runs/fetch-scte35-2023r1-pdf.txt, runs/webfetch-attempts.txt). The standard was read from Comcast/scte35-go@06d0ba5 docs/SCTE_35_2023r1.pdf with the agent's stdlib PDF text tool (123 pages, runs/derive_all.txt). The latest HLS draft is draft-pantos-hls-rfc8216bis-22 (datatracker API, runs/fetch-datatracker-rfc8216bis.txt).
open_issues: ANSI/SCTE 35-1 2023r2 and SCTE 35-2 2026 were not read: SCTE's catalogue returned 403. The layout in the survey is 2023r1's. Someone with a browser should check 35-1 against scte35.md §3, and check 35-2's event descriptor.

The PDF text came from the agent's own extractor, since no PDF tool is installed and installing one would write outside the output dir. The sample strings are confirmed by their CRC and by scte35-go's identical copies; other table text rests on that extraction alone.
Only one public VOD SCTE-35 stream was found, and it is generated on request by a vendor demo whose stability is unknown.

Licences: whether vectors from 'All Rights Reserved' sources (SCTE, Wowza, Unified, Google Ad Manager), from pages with no stated licence (AWS, broadpeak.io) or from threefive (GPL-2.0) may be committed to GPL-3.0-or-later Mirage is the owner's to settle, as with D-008. The fetched copies under scte35_evidence/downloads are third-party content and are not meant for commit.

Design choices for the owner (scte35.md §4.4): which time anchor takes precedence (position, START-DATE via PDT, or splice PTS), which segmentation_type_ids count as cue-out and cue-in, which duration takes precedence, what to do when the CRC fails, and how to handle cancelled events. The agent's recommendations are labelled as such.

Differences from D-070 to report: EXT-X-SCTE35, EXT-X-SPLICEPOINT-SCTE35 and Adobe's EXT-X-CUE are not in its list. The one public VOD stream found carries SCTE-35 in its segments as ID3 timed metadata, not as a 0x86 stream.

MEASUREMENT PENDING: whether FFmpeg's hls/mpegts demuxers deliver a 0x86 SCTE-35 stream or a timed-ID3 stream through mirage_vmaf's input and discard settings. No public HLS stream with a 0x86 PID was found to test this.
Unverified: how fMP4 packagers relate the source's 90 kHz splice PTS to the tracks' timescale and tfdt. No source read specifies #EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35 or the CUE tags normatively.
